tasks.title: Write tests for ink-vs-background masks
tasks.brief:
Create only tests/test_ink.py. Do not create or edit any handmetrics/ file or tests/conftest.py.

API under test (import inside each test function, not at module top-level):
  from handmetrics.ink import mask
  mask(image) -> numpy.ndarray of dtype bool, shape (H, W), True where ink is present.
image is a PIL Image (RGB or L) or an HxWx3 / HxW numpy array.

Expected values must come from images the test constructs, never from running mask() and recording the output.

Cover at least:
1. Synthetic clean scan: white background, black filled rectangle at a known box. Assert True exactly (or with a 1px antialias slop) on that box and False outside. Count True pixels from the geometry the test drew, not from the function.
2. Synthetic photo-like: background gray ~180, stroke gray ~40, RGB. Assert the known stroke pixels are True and far-from-stroke background is False.
3. Uneven illumination: horizontal gradient background (e.g. 140 to 220) plus a dark stroke (~40) whose absolute gray may overlap the dark side of the gradient. Assert the stroke is ink and a background patch on the dark side of the gradient is not.
4. Empty / no-ink white image: all False.
5. Real sample: the test reads data/labels.csv, picks the first row whose IDENTITY is not blank/UNREADABLE and whose file exists under data/images/, opens it with PIL. Assert the mask has both True and False, shape equals image size, and mean grayscale of ink pixels is darker than mean grayscale of non-ink pixels (this expected relation is from the definition of ink, not from a captured mask).

Do not listdir data/images/. Do not modify data/. Do not import handmetrics.ink to compute expected pixel counts.
acceptance: pytest collects at least five tests from tests/test_ink.py
at least one synthetic geometry test and one real-image test
expected ink pixels are defined by construction or by the darker-than-background rule, not by snapshotting mask()

tasks.title: Write tests for vertical-stroke slant in degrees
tasks.brief:
Create only tests/test_slant.py. Do not create handmetrics/ files or shared fixtures files.

API under test (import inside each test function):
  from handmetrics.slant import degrees
  degrees(ink: np.ndarray) -> float
ink is a 2D bool mask, True=ink. Return value: dominant vertical-stroke slant in degrees; positive leans right; 0 is upright.

Helpers must live in this file. Font: /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (upright by construction). To binarize a render or a real JPEG, use a test-owned rule (e.g. grayscale < 128 for black-on-white renders; grayscale < mean for real photos). Do not import handmetrics.ink or any other implementation to compute expected angles. Shear in image coordinates with x' = x + y * tan(radians(angle)) so positive angle leans right.

Cover at least:
1. Synthetic upright: render a word with vertical stems (e.g. 'HILL') with DejaVuSans, binarize, assert abs(degrees(mask)) <= 3.0. Expected 0 comes from the upright font, not from a dry run.
2. Synthetic known shear: take that upright render, shear by +20° and by -15°, binarize each, assert recovered angle within 3.0° of the applied angle.
3. Real-image delta: read data/labels.csv, pick the first usable existing image, binarize with the test-owned rule, measure s0; shear the RGB image by +12°, binarize the same way, measure s1; assert abs((s1-s0) - 12) <= 5.0. The expected delta is the shear the test applied.
4. All-False mask returns 0.0 (do not raise).

Do not listdir data/images/. Do not snapshot implementation output as the expected number.
acceptance: pytest collects at least four tests from tests/test_slant.py
absolute expected angles come from the upright font and applied shears; real-image test asserts a delta, not an absolute ground-truth slant
tolerances are explicit and finite (3° synthetic, 5° real delta)

tasks.title: Write tests for typical pen width in pixels

Create only tests/test_thickness.py. No other files.

API under test (import inside each test function):
  from handmetrics.thickness import pixels
  pixels(ink: np.ndarray) -> float

4. Real-image thicken: open the first usable JPEG from data/labels.csv (test reads the CSV; do not listdir data/images/). Binarize with a test-owned rule (grayscale < mean). Let t0 = pixels(mask). Dilate the mask by 1 pixel (test-owned numpy/PIL dilation). Let t1 = pixels(dilated). Assert t1 - t0 is within [1.0, 3.5] (one pixel on each side is +2; allow slop). tasks.title: Write tests for ink and writing-area fractions
tasks.brief:
Create only tests/test_coverage.py. No other files.

API under test (import inside each test function):
  from handmetrics.coverage import ink_fraction, area_fraction
  ink_fraction(ink: np.ndarray) -> float
    Fraction of the axis-aligned bounding box of ink pixels that is ink, in [0, 1].
  area_fraction(ink: np.ndarray) -> float
    Fraction of the full image (H*W) occupied by that bounding box, in [0, 1].

Cover at least:
1. Synthetic: 100x50 False canvas with a filled 20x10 ink rectangle. Expected ink_fraction = 1.0 (the bbox is solid ink); expected area_fraction = (20*10)/(100*50) = 0.04. Assert with abs err <= 1e-6.
2. Synthetic sparse bbox: two ink pixels at (0,0) and (9,9) on a 10x10 canvas. bbox is the whole image so area_fraction = 1.0; ink_fraction = 2/100 = 0.02. abs err <= 1e-6.
3. Scale invariance: nearest-neighbor 2x scale of a synthetic ink drawing (or of a real binarized crop). Both fractions must stay within 0.05 absolute of the unscaled values because they are ratios. Expected 'unchanged' comes from the definition of a ratio, not from a dry run.
4. Real image: first usable JPEG from data/labels.csv, binarize with test-owned grayscale < mean. Assert both returns are finite and in (0, 1]. Then 2x nearest-neighbor scale the mask and assert each fraction changes by at most 0.05.
5. All-False: both return 0.0.

Do not import handmetrics.coverage or ink to compute expected ratios. Do not listdir data/images/.

tasks.title: Write tests for baseline position and drift
tasks.brief:
Create only tests/test_baseline.py. No other files.

API under test (import inside each test function):
  from handmetrics.baseline import position, slope
  position(ink: np.ndarray) -> float
    Baseline y in pixels from the top of the image (y increases downward).
  slope(ink: np.ndarray) -> float
    Baseline drift as dy/dx in image coordinates (y down). 0 is level. Positive means the baseline moves down as x increases.

Cover at least:
1. Synthetic level word: render 'HILL' with DejaVuSans at /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf onto a tall white canvas with a known top padding (e.g. draw at y=40). Binarize grayscale < 128. Expected position is near the glyph baseline, which the test controls by the draw y plus the font's ascent (ImageFont.getmetrics or equivalent on the same font object the test used — that is test-controlled, not implementation output). Assert abs(position(mask) - expected_y) <= 3.0 px. Assert abs(slope(mask)) <= 0.03.
2. Vertical shift: take that mask, pad/roll it down by 10 pixels. position must increase by 10 ± 1. Expected delta is the shift the test applied.
3. Known drift: take a level synthetic mask and apply a vertical shear y' = y + x * s with s = 0.1. Assert recovered slope is within 0.04 of 0.1. Expected slope is the shear the test applied.
4. Real-image shift: first usable JPEG from data/labels.csv, binarize with test-owned grayscale < mean. Roll/shift down by 8 px; position delta within 8 ± 2. Shear with s = 0.08; slope delta within 0.08 ± 0.05.
5. All-False: position 0.0 and slope 0.0.

Do not import handmetrics.baseline or ink to compute expected y or slope. Do not listdir data/images/.

tasks.title: Write tests for distribution report CLI and summaries
tasks.brief:
Create only tests/test_report.py. No other files.

API under test (import inside test functions, not at module top-level):
  from handmetrics.report import summarize, main
  summarize(values) -> dict with exactly the keys count, mean, std, p5, p25, p50, p75, p95.
    count is int length; mean is arithmetic mean; std is population stdev (ddof=0); pK is the Kth percentile.
  main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int  # 0 on success
CLI: python3 -m handmetrics report --limit N
stdout must contain one line per metric in this exact order and prefix, each with those stats in this key=value form:
  slant_deg count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
  thickness_px count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
  ink_fraction count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
  area_fraction count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
  baseline_px count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
  baseline_slope count=... mean=... std=... p5=... p25=... p50=... p75=... p95=...
It may print discard totals before that (values must come from load()'s discard list, not literals).
Sampling: first N usable records in manifest order (deterministic). count on each metric line equals N when N usable records exist.

Cover at least:
1. summarize on a list the test owns, e.g. [0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]. Expected mean=2.0 from sum/len; std from sqrt(mean of squared deviations from that mean); percentiles from the definition (numpy.percentile is allowed in the test as the definition of percentile, applied to the same list, not by calling summarize to see what it said). Assert count==5.
2. subprocess or main(['report','--limit','3']) against real data/: exit 0; six metric lines with those prefixes; each count=3; each printed mean/std/percentile is a finite float. Do NOT assert the numeric style values of the sample (no ground truth, and you must not run the metrics yourself to fill in expected numbers).
3. --limit missing -> non-zero exit.
4. summarize([]) -> count 0 and the numeric fields 0.0 (no raise).

Do not import metric modules to compute expected report numbers. Do not modify data/.
acceptance: pytest collects at least four tests from tests/test_report.py
numeric expectations for summarize are computed from a test-owned list; CLI tests check structure, count=N, and finite values only
output line prefixes and stat keys are specified so the implementer can match them
